source.title: Gemstones: A Model Suite for Multi-Faceted Scaling Laws
source.authors: Sean McLeish; John Kirchenbauer; David Yu Miller; Siddharth Singh; A. Bhatele; Micah Goldblum; Ashwinee Panda; Tom Goldstein

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some table and figure content is flattened, but the text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits scaling laws on its own language-model suite and reports that fitted prescriptions vary with model selection, training data, architecture, and fitting procedure. It also reports results bearing on extrapolation, model shape, and downstream predictability.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results from Gemstones and fits laws to its own held-out validation losses. Results cited from other papers are not recorded as rows. Benchmark fits and architecture comparisons are recorded where they measure versions in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own 22-shape suite (50M–2B) and fits Chinchilla-style Approach 1 and Approach 3 laws to held-out loss. Its own results show the compute-optimal exponent moving from about 0.46 to 0.97 with fitting approach, token subset, schedule ablation, embedding counting and model subsampling. That bears directly on V3 and V7. It also reports loss extrapolation (V1/V2), shape effects (V4) and loss-to-benchmark fits (V6). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that scaling-law prescriptions are highly sensitive to model selection, checkpoint choice and fitting procedure. Their convex-hull fit is more robust when optimal points are sparse. Deeper models give lower loss and higher benchmark accuracy per FLOP, but wider models train faster in GPU hours, a result tied to their tensor-parallel setup. Applicability declines for very different training setups.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a diverse Gemstones suite and compares multiple scaling-law fitting approaches; it does not reproduce the original Kaplan or Hoffmann training and fitting recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported prescriptions vary with parameter-count treatment, model and token sampling, fitting approach, cooldown, learning rate, token sampling frequency, and fitting hyperparameters. Width and depth affect loss and training-time optimality; the latter is cautioned to depend on the parallelism setup.

fits_no_version.finding: At ~equal FLOPs, deeper 1B and 2B models score higher average benchmark accuracy than wider ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model depth affects downstream accuracy at fixed compute.

fits_no_version.finding: Wider models are Pareto-optimal in GPU hours, with up to >200% time overspend for poor shapes, under tensor-only parallelism.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wall-clock-optimal allocation differs from FLOP-optimal allocation.

record.problems: The trained suite spans 50M to 2B parameters, limiting the scale range tested. Some table entries are flattened in the supplied text. Results about time-optimal shapes may depend on the study's tensor-parallel-only training setup. Extreme shapes showed loss spikes and required patches; the authors also report that some patched models diverged after 350B tokens.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result was intentionally left out. Cited results from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Power law over several orders of magnitude; separate N, D, C laws with the other two non-bottlenecking (range is only 50M–2B).
Extrapolation over orders of magnitude (tested only <1.8B to ~2B).
Allocation at compute budgets beyond ~1e21 FLOPs; independent training setups.
Loss at fixed parameter count; architecture details other than width/depth.
All of it: other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer.
Curvature away from a single power law is not examined directly.

missing.what: Approach 3 ablation slopes (0.6986, 0.7515, 0.6740, 0.6992; deltas within ±0.055) and Approach 3 no-embeds (0.7141 base; ablations 0.6929–0.7350). These show Approach 3 is less sensitive than Approach 1.
Laws refit on DCLM and FineWeb-Edu validation data differ minimally from Dolma: a data choice with small effect.
Leave-one-model-out refits give a narrow tokens/param band. Approach 1 is less sensitive than Approach 3.
6N FLOPs approximation miscounts true FLOPs substantially (ratio ~0.8–1.5) for off-standard aspect ratios.
Predicted loss is flat in overtraining factor around the optimum, so deviations cost little.

record.verdict_notes: Approach 1 prescriptions are close to Chinchilla's equal scaling, while Approach 3 on the same data gives a Kaplan-like ~0.70 exponent. That is itself V7 evidence. The 2B 'extrapolation' is only a small step beyond the fitted range. Appendix A.1 claims fits are robust to halving the LR, yet Table 1 shows a delta of 0.0552 for the LR ablation (0.1552 no-embeds). Extreme wide models needed patches and some diverged after 350B tokens. The cooldown ablation uses pre-patch runs.

versions.untested_parts: No broad sweep over several orders of magnitude in model size; the Gemstones suite ranges from 50M to 2B parameters. The paper does not separately report a complete power-law test varying parameters, tokens, and compute independently with the other two held non-bottlenecking.
Extrapolation is tested from models below 1.8B parameters to models above 1.8B, not over multiple orders of magnitude.
The compute-optimal prescriptions are tested within this model suite and training setup, not across a broad range of independent training setups or compute budgets.
The paper studies width and depth, but does not systematically vary all other architectural details.
Other modalities and regimes such as image, video, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, and transfer are not tested.
Downstream predictability is tested on the paper's selected benchmarks and Gemstones models, not generally across tasks or model families.
The paper tests sensitivity to several choices in its own fitting and experimental setup, but does not systematically vary every possible parameter-counting, data, or schedule choice.
